title: Lattice release gating scratch
content:
Context:
This is a personal scratchpad for the ‘lattice’ model-service flip. Goal is to sketch heuristics for a low-friction canary + gated rollout that mitigates spike regressions (latency, hallucination rate) while letting client cohorts progress quickly. Rough, fragmented — notes to self and a place to capture feedback from quick experiments.

Primary constraints and assumptions:
- Multi-variant gating: we have two compatible variants for the same semantic model (fp16-quantized and int8-optimized). Runtime can fall back automatically if capacity is tight.
- Targets: keep p95 latency delta <= +15% vs baseline, error rate <= baseline + 0.2% (absolute), hallucination/regression alert <= 1.5x baseline on eval prompts.
- Tenants: mix of PLG self-serve and enterprise. Enterprise tenants may require pinned version during warmup window.

High level plan (stages):
1) Shadow priming (0% traffic) — 2h
   - Route 100% of examples to shadow queue for KV priming; monitor KV cache hit rate and cold-start tokens.
   - Run synthetic warmup suite (30 prompts per tenant type) in shadow.
   - Exit criteria: KV hit > 60% for steady-state paths OR 2h elapsed.
2) Micro canary (0.5% global) — 1h
   - Choose small cohort of low-risk tenants (beta list) with opt-in flag.
   - Observe p50/p95/p99, tail CPU/GPU utilisation, memory pressure, and token spend.
   - Feature-flagged gradients: enable latency-sensitive routing for these tenants to collect both perf + quality metrics.
3) Staggered ramp (0.5 -> 3 -> 10%) — 3–6h per step
   - Ramp steps only after stable telemetry for previous step (30m steady-state window).
   - At each step evaluate gating matrix (see below).
4) Cohort expansion and pin negotiation (10 -> 50 -> 100%) — 12–48h
   - For enterprise tenants: surface opt-in pin via console (graceful pin window of 72h).
   - Automatic fallback policy for high-cost spikes: route to compatible cheaper variant and alert ops.

Gating matrix (quick checklist to pass from one stage to next):
- Latency: p95(new)/p95(old) <= 1.15, p99 <= 1.25 (for micro canary may tolerate slightly higher p99 if volume tiny).
- Errors: 5xx increase <= 0.2% absolute OR relative <= 1.2x baseline (whichever stricter).
- Quality: eval set score drop <= 1.0% absolute (use daily prompt set + edge prompt slice for hallucination checks).
- Resource: GPU mem pressure < 85% sustained, scheduling queue length < baseline + 20%.
- Cost: estimated token-unit cost per 1M tokens should not exceed baseline by >10% without signoff.
- Signals OK = green; partial degrade = amber (requires engineering signoff); red = immediate rollback.

Pinning and roll-forward rules:
- Pin if tenant requests deterministic behavior (enterprise). Pin period default 72h; can extend via console request.
- If a pinned tenant experiences regressions, provide immediate manual rollback to prior pinned version and create incident note.
- Roll-forward allowed after a successful A/B slice (50k tokens) and one stable night window (2am-6am in tenant region) of no regressions.

Warmup and KV considerations:
- Prefill KV cache for 3x median session length observed for target tenant cohort.
- For multi-variant families, maintain a short-lived warm cache shared across variants (where allowed) to shorten cold-start cliffs.
- Track warmup effectiveness by measuring first-20-token latency vs tokens 20-100. Target reduction >= 25%.

Monitoring/observability checklist (what I watch during canary):
- Telemetry streams: p50/p95/p99 latency per model-variant, per-region, per-tenant.
- Quality probes: run small nightly regression sweep on 200 curated prompts (store diffs).
- Anomaly hooks: deploy alerts for sudden >0.5x increase in hallucination score or >1% absolute error spike.
- Cost telemetry: per-tenant token economy; immediate alert if spike >15% of expected billing rate.
- Heatmap: traffic vs latency by queue slot to detect scheduling backpressure.

Rollback plan (fast):
- Trigger: any red gating signal or SLA exceedance.
- Steps: 1) Flip routing to previous model variant for affected cohorts (SDK toggle). 2) Rehydrate KV cache for prior variant if pinned. 3) Postmortem stub: ownership, timeline, root-cause hypothesis, immediate mitigation.
- Communication: post to #deploys with snapshot of metrics + link to rollback PR. Notify customer success for enterprise tenants.

Open questions / TODOs:
- Should micro-canary cohorts be selected dynamically (by recent error stability) or manually maintained list? Pros/cons: dynamic reduces stale cohorts but risks surprising tenants.
- Evaluate whether fallback routing should prefer lower-cost variant or higher-stability variant by default. Add config knob in Console.
- Build small simulator to estimate p95 change given warmup percentage; ticketing: JIRA-8799.
- Need an easy console toggle for ‘force-warm’ for a tenant for 24h during ramp.

Quick action items (me):
- Draft a short PR for console toggle UX (small mock + API flag). Target: demo to PM Friday.
- Run a simulated warmup experiment on staging with 4 tenants and capture KV hit-time series.
- Schedule 30m sync with Ava + Diego to vet gating thresholds and make them tenant-aware.

Notes to self (random):
- Keep the canary window longer for variants that introduce kernel-level changes (e.g., new attention kernel).
- For small tenants, single-token regressions can look noisy — aggregate by session not single call.
- Save snapshots of the nightly regression diffs every day for 7 days to detect slow drifts.

End of scratchpad.
(If this drifts towards a polished playbook, move to shared_drives/product/console-and-rollouts and create an RFC.)
